text: Benazir Ahmed, a retired police officer, served as the 28th inspector general of the Bangladesh Police, appointed in April 2020. Prior to this, he was the director general of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) from January 2015 to April 2020, succeeding Mukhlesur Rahman. Born in Gopalganj, he completed his SSC exams in 1978 from SM Model High School and HSC exams in 1980 from Jagannath College, both in second division. He earned his undergraduate degree in 1982 and a master’s in English literature from the University of Dhaka in 1982, followed by a Ph.D. in business administration from the same university, with enrollment qualifications relaxed by his supervisor, Shibli Rubayat Ul Islam. Ahmed joined the Bangladesh Police Service as assistant superintendent of police in 1988 and held various positions, including commissioner of Dhaka Metropolitan Police. In 2013, he criticized a Transparency International Bangladesh report on the police, calling it "cruelly" and "unjustly" critical. On 30 December 2014, he was appointed director general of RAB. In 2022, the Home Ministry announced a 9-day visit to Germany for the inspection of 100,000 bed sheets and pillows for the police, which sparked controversy and was later canceled after public outcry, with the Bangladesh Police claiming the reports were "untrue and misleading" due to "linguistic confusion." On 10 December 2021, the U.S. Department of the Treasury added Ahmed to its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list under the Global Magnitsky Act, restricting financial dealings with him and blocking his assets. Ahmed denied all allegations, attributing the sanctions to "propaganda" and "anti-state forces," and accused human rights organizations—specifically one with a "Pakistani" South Asia director—of misleading U.S. politicians. An Interpol Red Notice was issued against him for crimes against humanity and economic corruption. In April 2024, Bangladesh Pratidin and Kaler Kantho published articles titled "Benazirer Ghore Aladiner Cherag" and "Boner Jomite Benazirer Resort," alleging Ahmed had amassed illegal wealth. The articles claimed he built the Savannah Eco Resort in Bairagitol village, Gopalganj, by illegally seizing land from Hindu families. On 23 May 2024, a court ordered the freezing of his properties and bank accounts over corruption charges. On 3 June 2024, he left the country. Transparency International Bangladesh raised alarms over the corruption allegations, and the Anti-Corruption Commission stated that evidence of corruption had been found and a case would be filed. On 12 June 2024, the court ordered the confiscation of additional properties of Ahmed and his family. Ahmed is married to Zeeshan Mirza and has three daughters: Farheen Rishta Binte Benazir, Tahseen Raisa Binte Benazir, and Zahra Zareen Binte Benazir.
